one_month_reasoning: No company-scheduled catalyst falls between 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-30: Q2 FY27 was reported 2026-09-02 and Q3 FY27 results (quarter ends Oct 31) will not come until roughly early December; BUILD developer event is typically November. Post-earnings drift has already played out: the stock spiked to $384.56 intraday after the Sep 2 print and has since consolidated in a $304-$349 weekly range, closing the week of Sep 28 at $342.5 (Twelve Data weekly series). A cluster of Form 4 / Form 144 insider sale filings in mid/late September is routine 10b5-1 selling, not a signal. Hyperscaler earnings (late October: MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL cloud growth) and CPI/FOMC prints can move software multiples but give no directional edge. So I stay close to a symmetric lognormal around today's $337.5 with a very slight upward drift (median ~$338.5) and monthly sigma ~16% (a bit below the 62%/3.5 = 17.7% implied by realized vol, since that figure is inflated by two large earnings-day gaps in May and September).

fair_value.method: Blend of EV/NTM sales (12.5x ~$9.6B NTM revenue at Sep-2027 -> $314), NTM non-GAAP P/E (80x ~$4.00 -> $320) and adjusted FCF yield (50x ~$2.4B NTM adj. FCF -> $314), each on ~390M diluted shares with ~$2.5B net cash; weights 0.4/0.3/0.3 give ~$316 twelve months out.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: NTM (Oct-27 to Sep-28) total revenue ~$9.6B x 12.5x EV/NTM sales = $120B EV, + ~$2.5B net cash = $122.5B equity / 390M diluted shares

inputs_detail.value: $9.0B RPO (+30%), ~54% (~$4.9B) recognized in 12 months to Jul-2027

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $6.32B; product revenue is ~96% of total (Q2: $1.49B of $1.55B), so $6.07B/0.96 ~ $6.33-6.35B.

Exit growth 37-38% in Q3 guide, NRR 126%, RPO +30% and management's 'observed behavior' guidance (no change in methodology) support ~30% for FY28 with normal deceleration to ~25% in FY29; this lands product revenue near ~$9.9B in FY29, i.e. at/above the long-standing $10B FY29 product-revenue target reiterated at the June 2026 investor day.
~1/3 weight FY28 run-rate exit quarter plus ~2/3 FY29 first three quarters on the estimates above.

Today: ~$128B diluted market cap (380M guided diluted shares x $337.5) less ~$2B net cash ~ $126B EV on ~$7.6B NTM revenue ~ 16.5x for ~35% growth. With growth decelerating toward ~25% by late 2027, I compress roughly in proportion to growth (about 0.5x EV/sales per point of growth).
Jul-31-2026 cash $1.71B + ST investments $0.64B + LT investments $1.98B = $4.33B less convertible notes $2.28B = ~$2.05B; add ~ $0.5B of retained FCF after buybacks/tax on net settlement.
FY27 non-GAAP diluted share guide 380M (Q3 382M, includes ~10M convert shares); 352.8M basic outstanding at Aug 21 2026; add ~2.5% annual net dilution from SBC with only $300M bought back in H1 FY27.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Sep-2027 ~$4.00 x 80x

inputs_detail.derivation: FY28 ~$8.25B revenue x ~17.5% non-GAAP op margin (Q2 15.3% with +400bp y/y expansion, management targets GAAP profitability by Q4 FY28) + ~$0.15B interest, ~20% tax -> ~$1.3B / 390M ~ $3.3; FY29 ~$10.3B x ~20% -> ~$4.4; NTM blend ~$4.0.

Stock trades at ~152x FY27 consensus EPS ($337.5/$2.22) and ~100x my FY28; with EPS growing ~35-40% I use a PEG of ~2 on forward growth, i.e. ~80x, a multiple consistent with where high-growth infra software traded during 2026 (SNOW itself was ~65x forward at the April low of $118 on then-lower estimates).

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM adjusted FCF at Sep-2027 ~$2.4B x 50x (2% yield) = $120B + ~$2.5B net cash / 390M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: ~24-25% adj. FCF margin (FY27 guide 23%, June 2026 investor day frames rising FCF and falling SBC % of revenue) on ~$9.6B NTM revenue.
Today ~$126B EV / ~$1.75B NTM adj. FCF ~ 72x. Adjusted FCF excludes ~29% of revenue in SBC, so I haircut the multiple as growth slows toward 25%; 50x is roughly 2x the FCF growth rate.

bear.story: AI-driven acceleration proves a one-to-two quarter pull-forward: consumption growth slips back to the high-20s by mid-2027, FY28 guide in Feb-2027 comes in ~24-25%, product gross margin keeps sliding below 74% on lower-margin AI inference (frontier-model costs, $390M AI-provider commitment), and software multiples re-rate as they did in Feb-Apr 2026 when the stock fell to $118. ~8-9x NTM sales.

base.story: Growth decelerates gracefully from 37% to ~28-30% through FY28, operating margin expands toward ~17-18%, GAAP profitability on track for Q4 FY28; multiple compresses from ~16.5x to ~12.5-13x NTM sales but estimate growth carries the price modestly above today.

bull.story: CoCo/CoWork and Cortex keep compounding (AI already ~half of the acceleration), growth holds in the mid-30s into FY28, product revenue tracks well ahead of the $10B FY29 target, margins expand despite AI mix; market pays ~16-17x NTM sales on ~$10B+. Stock reaches the $479-531 CEO-PSU tranche zone.

thesis_break_reason: Around $215 (-36%) the stock would be back below where it traded before the Q1 FY27 re-acceleration print (May 2026, ~$172-255) and would imply ~9x NTM sales, i.e. the market no longer believes AI is additive to consumption. Ordinary 60%-vol noise rarely takes a name that far without a fundamental trigger such as a guide-down, product growth falling under ~28%, NRR dropping below ~120%, or product gross margin breaking toward 70% on AI costs.

Snowflake BUILD developer conference: CoCo / CoWork / Cortex product updates

Q4 FY27 results and first FY28 product revenue / margin guidance; Q4-weighted renewals and RPO
Expiry of the $4.5B total buyback authorization (extended to March 2027); renewal or not
Snowflake Summit and possible investor-day update of FY29/FY31 targets
Q2 FY28 results, one month before horizon

key_uncertainties: Durability of the AI-driven acceleration (management says AI products drove ~half the acceleration) vs one-off migration/pull-forward
Product gross margin erosion from AI mix: FY27 guide lowered to 74% from prior, vs 78% long-term target; minimum AI-provider commitment raised to $390M
Multiple sensitivity: stock moved from $118 to $384 in five months; software sentiment swings (AI-disruption-of-SaaS fears) dominate at ~16x sales
Dilution: SBC ~29% of revenue, only $300M repurchased in H1 FY27, ~10M convert shares
Competitive pressure from Databricks and hyperscalers, and open table formats (Iceberg) lowering switching costs, as flagged in the 10-Q risk factors
reasoning: Primary documents show a genuinely re-accelerating business: Q2 FY27 product revenue $1.49B +37% (third straight acceleration), Q3 guide +37-38%, FY27 guide raised to $6.07B (+36%) from $5.84B, non-GAAP op margin raised to 14.5%, RPO $9.0B +30% with 54% due in 12 months, NRR 126%, 692 net new customers (+32%). Footnotes the recaps skip cut both ways: product gross margin slipped to 71% GAAP (74% non-GAAP guide, lower than before) because new AI capabilities have not reached scale; the 10-Q discloses a raised $390M minimum commitment to a third-party AI provider and an amended $6.0B five-year cloud commitment (confidence in demand, but fixed cost); buybacks were only $300M in H1 and SBC is ~29% of revenue; the July 2026 CEO PSU sets price hurdles at $324/$375/$427/$479/$531, so the board sees ~$375-430 as a 3-5 year goal rather than a near-term one; June investor day guides to GAAP profitability in Q4 FY28 and falling SBC. Valuation: at $337.5 the stock is ~16.5x NTM EV/sales, ~150x FY27 EPS and ~72x NTM adj. FCF. Rolling estimates forward to Sep-2027 (FY28 ~$8.25B, FY29 ~$10.3B revenue) and compressing multiples as growth fades to ~25% gives ~$316 fair value, slightly below spot; sell-side average targets (~$425-435, 32 of 35 Buy) are well above, reflecting momentum and estimate revisions. I centre the 12-month distribution with a median ~ $340 (a small positive drift balancing my below-spot fundamental value against strong revision momentum and consensus), and use a lognormal sigma ~0.47 (between the 62% realized vol, which includes two earnings gaps and the April drawdown, and ~40-45% typical for high-growth software) with a slightly fatter left tail since this exact stock fell 45% within the past year on sector de-rating. Scenario mean ($350) sits a little above spot. Research limits: transcript fetched via a Yahoo copy (Benzinga blocked), the investor-day PDF chart numbers were not text-extractable (used its readable captions), and Twelve Data / Alpha Vantage estimate endpoints were unavailable, so consensus beyond FY27 is my own estimate. No option data used.
